## Recommendation
- **Go to Muskegon.** My expected boat ratings this week (0-4 scale): **Muskegon 3, South Haven 3, St. Joseph 3, Grand Haven 2.** These come from the latest reports, which are 13 days old.
- Start around 70-120 ft of water, with lines about 35-90 ft down. Move out to 150-220 ft if the bite is there.
- Run green and orange spoons, glow spoons in low light, and white flashers with green or white flies.
- Check the wind before you leave. The last week was gusty, so if it's blowing hard, wait for a calmer day rather than run the lake in a small boat.

## Why
- Muskegon's Aug 7 boat reports rated both Chinook and coho good (3) at 35-90 ft down, so it's my top pick (Muskegon, 2024-08-07).
- South Haven matched Muskegon on Chinook and coho (both 3), but its best water was a narrow 90 ft (South Haven, 2024-08-07).
- St. Joseph's only boat line was rated excellent (4) at 100 ft, but it wasn't split by species and the report said that week was slower than the one before (St. Joseph, 2024-08-07). I'd expect it to be strong, but I rate it 3 until a newer report confirms it.
- Grand Haven's species lines were below average (Chinook 1, coho 2), so I rate it lowest (Grand Haven, 2024-08-07).
- I'd expect fish to be deeper than the surface, since buoy surface water is about 70-73 F and salmon prefer 52-58 F (NY DEC guidance, general reference).

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (all Aug 7, 2024 unless noted; the Jul 31 reports are the only other recent boat data)
- Muskegon: Chinook good (3) and coho good (3), "70-220 ft" of water, "35 to 90 feet down," glow spoons in green and orange. The unspecified line was 1 (Muskegon, 2024-08-07).
- South Haven: coho good (3) and Chinook good (3), "the best location being 90 feet of water," spoons most productive (South Haven, 2024-08-07).
- St. Joseph: boat, "salmon fishing continued to be very good at around 100 feet," rated 4, spoons best with flies and meat rigs also catching fish (St. Joseph, 2024-08-07).
- Grand Haven: unspecified boat line 3, but Chinook 1 and coho 2, "70-230 ft," spoons and white flashers (Grand Haven, 2024-08-07).
- Jul 31 for context: Muskegon good (3) at 70-150 ft, South Haven good (3) at 80-90 ft, St. Joseph good (3) with the best water "well beyond 120 feet" (2024-07-31).

**Past seasons** (history, not current; matched on similar buoy temperature near this date)
- Similar weeks in 2022-2023 ranged from slow to good. Grand Haven was good (3) at 80-160 ft in Aug 2023 (Grand Haven, 2023-08-09), and Muskegon was good (3) at 90-130 ft in Aug 2023 (Muskegon, 2023-08-02).
- The slow weeks were St. Joseph in late August 2023, with "hard time locating fish" (St. Joseph, 2023-08-23) and "very few anglers" out due to poor weather (St. Joseph, 2023-08-30).

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a summary for the week before Aug 20, not live data; no live forecast was available)
- Buoy surface water was about 70-73 F. At South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon it fell 15-18 F over the week and was flagged as possible upwelling. St. Joseph dropped 4 F with no flag.
- Upwelling-type north-to-east wind ran 54-64 hours in the week before at South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon, and 57 hours at St. Joseph.
- Wind averaged about 10 mph with gusts of 28-34 mph.
- I'd expect the cold water to have pushed fish shallower near Grand Haven and Muskegon, but that's my inference and the reports don't confirm it.

## Caveats
- The newest boat reports are from Aug 7, 2024, 13 days old. Use them as a guide and check with local bait shops or a current DNR report.
- Live weather and water data weren't available. The water and wind figures come from the week before today, not a forecast.
- The Aug 7 report was split across species lines, and St. Joseph's rating came from an unspecified-species line, so the port comparison is thin.

- DNR bulletin, Jul 31, 2024 (for context): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3abfd6e
